# task-abfafb66: Fill aligned rectangle between boundary stripes

## Trigger
Use for recurring task-abfafb66 grids with a full horizontal color-2 stripe and matching-color marker runs along the top and/or bottom boundaries. Re-derive positions from current input; do not hard-code demo dimensions or colors.

## Demonstrated behavior
Fill cells with color 4 in the otherwise-empty region lying vertically between the color-2 horizontal line and the boundary marker run(s), aligned to the columns occupied by the matching boundary markers. Preserve all original cells, including the marker runs and stripe. The boundary marker pattern(s) determine the horizontal span of the fill; the color-2 line bounds its vertical extent. The fill reaches the boundary-adjacent rows between stripe and boundary markers and is contiguous, even when the marker run is on the opposite side of the stripe.

## Evidence
- Demo 1, 9x4: top boundary row `0 3 3 3`; color-2 full stripe at row 4; bottom boundary row `3 3 0 0`. Output added color 4 in rows 1–3, column 1 (0-indexed), leaving all else unchanged. This is the overlap of the top/bottom marked spans: top columns 1–3 and bottom columns 0–1.
- Demo 2, 13x5: top boundary has color 6 in columns 1–4; stripe at row 6; bottom boundary has color 6 in columns 2–4. Output added a 3-column-wide rectangle of 4s at columns 2–4, rows 1–5. This confirms the intersection of marked column ranges and filling the whole gap between boundary and stripe, not only a one-cell-thick line.
- Solved test: 11x5, top boundary color 7 across columns 0–4; stripe at row 5; bottom boundary color 7 in columns 1–2. Output was 4 in columns 1–2, rows 1–4, preserving boundaries and stripe. Accepted correct.

## Procedure
1. Find the full horizontal row of 2s.
2. Identify boundary rows (typically first/last) containing a nonzero marker color other than 2; infer marked column spans from them.
3. Use the common/intersecting columns indicated by aligned top/bottom marker runs, as exemplified by the demos.
4. Fill with 4 in the zero-valued cells between the stripe and the marked boundary rows, excluding both boundary rows and stripe.
5. Preserve every input cell otherwise and validate dimensions.

## Caution
Only two demos establish the overlap behavior; demo 1 has different top/bottom marker spans, so using their intersection explains its single-column result. The test had a full-width top marker run and a narrower bottom run, again yielding the narrower span. If a fresh instance has only one marked boundary, disjoint runs, interior obstacles, or multiple stripe rows, request additional evidence rather than extrapolating confidently."
}
